top_opportunities.title: hy-check: generic function call results are untyped — var s string = id(3), take_string(id(3)), id(3) == "a" pass check, fail go build (HYB-E1002)
top_opportunities.description:
### Summary

The result of a call to a **generic** top-level function is untyped to `hyb check`. `call_result_kinds` (`buildable.rs`, `Expr::Ident` arm) runs `kind_of_ty` on the declared result type. For `fn id[t any](v t) t`, that result type is the type parameter `t`. `kind_of_named("t")` returns `OpKind::Unknown`, and every operand guard treats `Unknown` as fail-open. So a generic call result passes every var-init, argument, return, comparison and arithmetic check, and the emitted Go then fails `go build`.

This is not #2812 (uninferable type parameters), #1961 (argument types of explicit `id[int](...)` calls), #729 (constraint enforcement) or #2490 (shape erasure for the loan/freeze passes). Here the type argument is known, either inferred from the arguments or given explicitly, but it is never substituted into the result.

### Reproducer (hyb built from main b3f9d61, go1.26.9)

Each line below is its own `main` in a separate file, with `fn id[t any](v t) t { return v }`, `fn first[t any](a []t) t { return a[0] }`, `fn wrap[t any](v t) []t { return []t{v} }` and `fn take(s string) {}` declared at top level.

|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `var s string = id(3)` | OK (0 diagnostics) | `cannot use id(3) (value of type int) as string value in variable declaration` |
| 2 | `x := id(3); var s string = x` | OK | `cannot use x (variable of type int) as string value in variable declaration` |
| 3 | `take(id(3))` | OK | `cannot use id(3) (value of type int) as string value in argument to take` |

top_opportunities.title: hy-check: calls through fn values from index, struct field or call result (fs[0]("a"), v.cb("a"), mk()(1, 2), var s string = m["a"](1)) skip arity, argument and result checks (HYB-E1002)
top_opportunities.description:
### Summary

When the callee is an **expression** that yields a fn value, `hyb check` checks nothing about the call: not the arity, not the argument types, and not the result kind. The affected callees are:

- an indexed slice/map element: `fs[0](...)`, `m["a"](...)`
- a struct fn field: `v.cb(...)`
- the result of another call: `mk()(...)`

Calls through a named closure local or a fn-typed parameter are covered by #2845 (PR #2846). Inline literal calls `(fn(x int) {...})(...)` are covered by #1877. This issue covers the remaining callee shapes.

### Reproducer (hyb built from main b3f9d61, go1.26.9)

`fn mk() fn(int) int { return fn(x int) int { return x } }` and `struct h { cb fn(int) int }` are declared at top level. Each row is a separate file.

| # | Hybrid | `hyb check` | `go vet` on the emitted Go |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `fmt.println(mk()("a"))` | OK (0 diagnostics) | `cannot use "a" (untyped string constant) as int value in argument to mk()` |
| 2 | `fmt.println(mk()(1, 2))` | OK | `too many arguments in call to mk()` |
| 3 | `var s string = mk()(1)` | OK | `cannot use mk()(1) (value of type int) as string value in variable declaration` |
| 4 | `x := mk()(1); fmt.println(x + "a")` | OK | `invalid operation: x + "a" (mismatched types int and untyped string)` |
| 5 | `fs := []fn(int) int{...}; fmt.println(fs[0]("a"))` | OK | `cannot use "a" (untyped string constant) as int value in argument to fs[0]` |
| 6 | `m := map[string]fn(int) int{...}; var s string = m["a"](1)` | OK | `cannot use m["a"](1) (value of type int) as string value in variable declaration` |
| 7 | `v := h{cb: ...}; fmt.println(v.cb("a"))` | OK | `cannot use "a" (untyped string constant) as int value in argument to v.cb` |

### Root cause

`buildable.rs`:
- `call_result_kinds` has arms for `FnLit`, `Ident` and `Field` (methods and option payloads only). An `Expr::Call`, `Expr::Index` or fn-typed struct-field callee falls through to `None`, so its result is `Unknown`.
- `check_call_operands` o
